description: The complete cathode-ray-tube diagram printed with Question 10. A points to the cathode, B to the cylindrical anode, and C to the screen; the high-voltage supply, electron beam and vacuum are also labelled.
The complete three-pin-plug photograph printed with Question 11. The three arrows and boxed labels A, B and C are all fully visible.
The task-relevant A/B wiring detail from the electrical-plug diagram printed with Question 9(c). A points to the earth wire and B points to the live wire; the fuse and both arrows are fully visible.

The complete calorimetry apparatus diagram printed with Question 3. A points to the thermometer and B to the surrounding lagging or insulation; the calorimeter, crushed ice, water and cloth are fully labelled.
The complete stationary-wave diagram printed with Question 10(iii), showing the fundamental mode in a pipe closed at one end. X marks the antinode at the open end and Y the node at the closed end.

The complete velocity-time graph printed with Question 7. It rises from A to B, remains constant from B to C, drops sharply when the parachute opens at C, then settles to the small landing velocity after D.

labelMeanings.meaning: start of the first constant-velocity interval
start of the low landing-velocity interval

description: The complete gold-leaf-electroscope diagram printed with Question 14(c). The cap, insulating plug, frame and earth connection are visible, and X points to the gold leaf.
